items.title: 2.2.2 Intersection of Two Linear Functions (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Pichle sabaq mein ek line aur axes ka milna dekha. Ab do lines ek doosre ko kahan kaat'ti hain, yeh dekhenge. Yeh asal mein do simultaneous linear equations ko graph se hal karna hai, jo aap pichli classes mein algebra se karte aaye hain.

Kitab kehti hai: do linear functions ka point of intersection woh point hai jahan un ke graphs ek doosre ko cross karte hain. Is ka matlab hai ke us point par dono functions ki \(x\) aur \(y\) values same hoti hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Table of values mein yeh point pehchanna bohat aasan hai: woh \(x\) dhoondiye jis par dono \(y\) wale columns barabar ho jaayein. Wohi row milne ka point hai. Graph banane se pehle hi table aap ko jawab ka ishara de deta hai.
Ek aur baat: do alag seedhi lines bilkul ek point par milti hain. Sirf ek surat mein nahin miltin: jab woh parallel hon, yani un ka slope \(m\) same ho magar \(c\) alag. Jaise \(y = 2x + 1\) aur \(y = 2x + 5\) kabhi nahin miltin, rail ki do patriyon ki tarah.

blocks.title: Example 8
blocks.problem: Find the point of intersection of \(y = 3x + 2\) and \(y = -x + 6\).
steps:
Given: do linear functions \(y = 3x + 2\) aur \(y = -x + 6\).
To find: woh point jahan dono lines ek doosre ko kaat'ti hain.
Method: dono lines ke liye ek hi table banayenge (same \(x\) values ke saath), dono lines ek hi axes par kheenchenge aur milne wala point parhenge; yeh kitab ka tareeqa hai. Aakhir mein dono \(y\) barabar rakh kar algebra se check karenge.

Step 2: \(y = -x + 6\) ki values
\[x = -1:\ y = -(-1) + 6 = 7\]
\[x = 0:\ y = -0 + 6 = 6\]
\[x = 1:\ y = -1 + 6 = 5\]
Kyun: dono lines ke liye same \(x\) values is liye li hain ke hum har row mein dono \(y\) ka muqabla kar sakein.
Dhyan dein: \(-(-1) = +1\), is liye \(x = -1\) par \(y = 1 + 6 = 7\) aata hai. Yahan bohat se bachche \(5\) likh dete hain.

Step 3: Dono lines kheench kar milne ka point parhein
\((-1, -1), (0, 2), (1, 5)\) plot kar ke jorein; phir \((-1, 7), (0, 6), (1, 5)\) plot kar ke jorein (neeche table aur graph dekhiye). Dono lines \((1, 5)\) par ek doosre ko kaat'ti hain.
Kyun: table mein \(x = 1\) wali row mein dono columns \(y = 5\) de rahe hain. Matlab \((1, 5)\) dono lines par hai, aur do lines ka common point yahi hai. Ek line upar ja rahi hai (slope \(3\) positive) aur doosri neeche aa rahi hai (slope \(-1\) negative), is liye in ka kahin na kahin milna yaqeeni tha.

Tasdeeq:
Milne ke point par dono \(y\) barabar hote hain, is liye dono right-hand sides barabar rakhein:
\[3x + 2 = -x + 6\]
\[4x = 4 \Rightarrow x = 1\]
\[y = 3(1) + 2 = 5\]
Aur doosri line se bhi: \(-1 + 6 = 5\). Dono equations satisfy ho gayin, is liye \((1, 5)\) bilkul sahi hai.
blocks.answer: Dono lines ka point of intersection \((1, 5)\) hai.

blocks.caption: Table (kitab wala): y = 3x + 2 aur y = −x + 6 ki values

blocks.alt: Graph of the lines y = 3x + 2 and y = minus x + 6 on axes marked from minus 2 to 8 (x) and minus 3 to 7 (y). The table points (minus 1, minus 1), (0, 2) on the first line and (minus 1, 7), (0, 6) on the second are plotted; the lines cross at (1, 5).
blocks.caption: Figure: the lines y = 3x + 2 and y = −x + 6 meet at (1, 5) (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text: In points ko plot karne se saaf nazar aata hai ke \((1, 5)\) dono seedhi lines ka point of intersection hai, jaisa figure mein dikhaya gaya hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari practice hai (kitab ka sawal nahin): \(y = x + 1\) aur \(y = -2x + 7\).
Table: \(x = 0\): \(1\) aur \(7\); \(x = 1\): \(2\) aur \(5\); \(x = 2\): \(3\) aur \(3\).
\(x = 2\) par dono barabar hain, is liye milne ka point \((2, 3)\) hai.
Tasdeeq: \(x + 1 = -2x + 7 \Rightarrow 3x = 6 \Rightarrow x = 2\), aur \(y = 3\). Sahi!

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Agar table mein kisi bhi row mein dono \(y\) barabar na hon to kya karein? (Jawab: dekhiye ke farq kis taraf kam ho raha hai, aur us taraf aur \(x\) values le kar table barhaayein. Ho sakta hai milne ka point fraction wala ho, jaise \(x = 1.5\); tab algebra se pakki value nikaalein.)

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Milne ke point par dono lines ka \(x\) bhi same aur \(y\) bhi same hota hai.
2. Table mein yeh woh row hai jahan dono \(y\) columns barabar hon.
3. Algebraic check: dono right-hand sides barabar rakhein, \(x\) nikaalein, phir \(y\).
4. Same slope aur alag \(c\) wali lines parallel hoti hain; woh kabhi nahin miltin.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(-(-1)\) ko \(-1\) likh dena: \(y = -x + 6\) mein \(x = -1\) par jawab \(7\) hai.
2. Sirf ek line ka point utha lena: jawab dono equations ko satisfy kare, tabhi sahi hai.
3. Table itna chhota bana dena ke milne wala point us mein aaye hi nahin; zaroorat ho to table barhaayein.
4. Dono lines alag scale par banana; dono ek hi axes par aur ek hi scale par honi chahiyein.
